evidence._readme: The client that cannot hold a SuperDocs key. Its own shipped documentation defines `command`/`args`/`env` for stdio and `serverUrl` for SSE — and no headers field anywhere. Since SuperDocs authenticates with an Authorization header, the honest diagnosis is that the combination is not configurable. That is a finding worth reporting precisely, not a gap to work around.

darwin.how: ~/.gemini/config/mcp_config.json confirmed present on a real installation (Antigravity IDE.app installed). The file was 0 bytes — a fresh client with nothing configured, which is why config.file-empty exists as a distinct defect.

linux.how: Same ~/.gemini layout expected; no Linux installation available.

schema.how: Read from documentation SHIPPED WITH THE IDE — builtin/skills/agy-customizations/docs/mcp_servers.md — which is stronger than third-party docs but still not an observed config. It gives the container key `mcpServers`, stdio fields `command`/`args`/`env`, and the SSE field `serverUrl`. Grepping that document for header, auth, token, bearer and api-key returns NOTHING.
schema.capture_todo: If Antigravity later gains a headers mechanism, capture a real remote entry before changing any of this.

repairs.how: Not applicable while the client cannot carry a credential; nothing useful could be repaired.

write_capable._note: All false, and likely to stay false: with no header mechanism there is no working configuration to write.

locations.note: Global configuration, applying to all sessions. A second copy exists under ~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/, and plugins may carry their own mcp_config.json; only the documented global path is scanned.

server_map._shape_note: mcpServers, like Claude Code — but the entry shape inside is different, which is exactly why container key and entry schema are separate pieces of data.

transport._note: The only documented remote transport is SSE. SuperDocs answers in plain JSON with no SSE stream, so compatibility is NOT assumed here — it would need testing against a real Antigravity client before any claim is made.

headers.unsupported_reason: Antigravity's mcp_config.json schema documents no headers field for either transport, so there is no way to send Authorization: Bearer. SuperDocs requires one.

identification._host_rule: Exact host comparison only. Applied to serverUrl, not url.

repairs._readme: Deliberately empty in both lists. Nothing here is repairable while the client cannot carry a credential — planning repairs would imply a fix that cannot work.
